# Startup checks: fail fast without a git identity, and handle leftover task worktrees

## What to build

Two startup checks that stop a run **before any task starts** instead of letting it break partway with exit 2.

1. **Jira KAN-64 / GE-03 — no git identity.** When git has no author/committer identity (no `user.name`/`user.email` in repo-local, global or system config and no `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` env vars), every task burns its 3 attempts (the agent's `git commit` fails with `Author identity unknown ... fatal: unable to auto-detect email address`), the run aborts with exit 2 and leaves a `graph/<run-id>` branch, a `graph-task/<run-id>/1` branch and worktrees behind. `src/launch/preflight.ts` and `src/runner/startup.ts` have no identity check. New behaviour: the preflight refuses with a clear message telling the user to set `git config user.name` / `user.email`, before `.graph-execution/` or any branch is created. The check asks git itself (`git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` and `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` in the repo), so env vars, repo-local config, `includeIf`, `user.useConfigOnly` etc. are all respected exactly as `git commit` will see them. It covers a normal run, `--resume`, the detached `--web` launcher (it calls `preflight`) and the suite (`graph-execution suite` start and `suite --resume`).
2. **Jira KAN-70 / GE-09 — leftover worktree of the run's branches.** If a worktree (anywhere on disk) still has `graph-task/<run-id>/<n>` checked out, the task's `git worktree add -B graph-task/<run-id>/<n> ...` fails with `fatal: 'graph-task/<run-id>/2' is already used by worktree at '<path>'`, the task fails and the run exits 2 partway. Reproduced with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=<run-id>` (the suite uses this env var to start feature runs with a fixed id). New behaviour: **refuse at startup with cleanup steps; only reclaim what is provably safe.** Decision (made after reading `src/git/git.ts` and `src/cleanup/`): a leftover worktree can be anywhere, e.g. one the user created by hand with uncommitted work, so removing it with `--force` could destroy data; we do NOT delete it. The only automatic reclaim is `git worktree prune`, which only forgets registrations whose directory no longer exists (git still blocks `-B` on a branch "checked out" in such a missing worktree — verified with git 2.43). On `--resume` of the same run, the run's own worktrees under `<runDir>/worktrees/` (task-*, integration, review-*) are legitimate and must not be refused; only worktrees of the run's branches **outside** that folder are refused.

Layers touched: `src/git/git.ts` (two small helpers), `src/launch/preflight.ts` (the checks, wired into `checkEnvironment` and `preflightResume`), `src/runner/startup.ts` (leftover check for a new run), `src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (identity check once per suite and on suite resume), plus regression tests.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/launch/preflight.ts` (lines 67–91) — `checkEnvironment` and `checkRepo`: the git/config/provider checks shared by `preflight` (normal run, detached launcher, suite) and `startup`. The identity check goes into `checkEnvironment` right after the "no commits yet" check (lines 71–76).
- `src/launch/preflight.ts` (lines 117–167) — `preflight` and `preflightResume`: resume path (no `checkEnvironment` call there). The identity and leftover-worktree checks for resume go here, after `StateStore.load` (line 149).
- `src/runner/startup.ts` (lines 51–82) — `startup()`: computes the run id (`forced ?? generateRunId()`, line 73), refuses an existing `state.json` (lines 74–77), then `mkdir(runDir)` (line 78). The leftover check goes between lines 77 and 78 so nothing is created on refusal.
- `src/git/git.ts` (lines 1–57) — the `git()` helper (line 7), `addWorktree` (lines 38–41, uses `worktree add -B` with a base), `removeWorktreeIfPresent` (lines 51–57); `pruneWorktrees` (lines 162–165); `resolveRef` (lines 130–134); `listBranches` (lines 140–149, pattern for a `reject: false` git call). New helpers go here.
- `src/cleanup/scan.ts` (lines 58–68) — `checkedOutWorktrees`: existing parser of `git worktree list --porcelain`; mirror it (do not refactor scan.ts).
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 115–117) — `integrationBranchName(runId) = graph/<runId>`, `taskBranchName(runId, taskId) = graph-task/<runId>/<taskId>`; (line 179) `createBranch(ctx.repo, ctx.startingCommit, integrationBranch)` fails if `graph/<runId>` already exists; (lines 678–687) the task `prepare` step that calls `addWorktree(..., branch, base)` and fails on a leftover worktree; (lines 209–227) `resume()`: `preflight({resume: true})` → lock → `reconcile`.
- `src/state/resume.ts` (lines 35–66) — `reconcile`: on resume it prunes and removes every worktree in `<runDir>/worktrees/` except `integration`. That is why the run's own worktrees are fine on resume.
- `src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (lines 120–141) — `validateSuite` runs `preflight` per feature inside a loop that prefixes errors with the feature name (lines 133–139); (lines 195–199) `resumeSuite` starts with `repoRoot(opts.cwd)` and calls no preflight.
- `src/launch/preflight.test.ts` (lines 1–65) — test pattern: `tempRepo()`, `refuses()` helper that also asserts `.graph-execution` was not created.
- `src/runner/startup.test.ts` (lines 1–86) — test pattern for `startup()` with `env: { GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID: ... }` and `createFakeProvider({})`.
- `src/cli.test.ts` (lines 12–19, 86–94) — CLI test pattern (runs `dist/cli.js`, built by `vitest.global-setup.ts`): "exits 2 with a clear error ... before creating a run".
- `src/state/resume.test.ts` (lines 1–68) and `src/__fixtures__/resume.ts` (lines 38–88) — `withRepo(config, script, fn)`, `start(repo)`, `resumeCli(repo)`, `onlyRun(repo)`, `readState(runDir)`.
- `src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts` (lines 1–10, 109–116) — suite test pattern ("rejects fewer than 2 features before creating anything"), fixtures in `src/__fixtures__/suite.ts` (`withRepo`, `addFeature`, `commitAll`, `cliPath`).
- `src/__fixtures__/repo.ts` — `tempRepo()` sets a **repo-local** identity (`user.name Test`, `user.email test@example.com`); tests for a missing identity must unset it.

## Patterns to follow

**Git helper with `reject: false` (src/git/git.ts:140-149):**
```typescript
export async function listBranches(repo: string, prefix: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const res = await execa("git", ["for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", `refs/heads/${prefix}`], {
    cwd: repo,
    reject: false,
  });
  if (res.exitCode !== 0) return [];
  return res.stdout.split("\n").map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
}
```

**Porcelain worktree parsing (src/cleanup/scan.ts:58-68):**
```typescript
const res = await execa("git", ["worktree", "list", "--porcelain"], { cwd: repo, reject: false });
if (res.exitCode !== 0) return [];
let current = "";
for (const line of res.stdout.split("\n")) {
  if (line.startsWith("worktree ")) current = line.slice("worktree ".length).trim();
  else if (line.startsWith("branch refs/heads/")) out.push({ branch: line.slice("branch refs/heads/".length).trim(), path: current });
}
```
`git worktree list --porcelain` prints one block per worktree (`worktree <path>`, `HEAD <sha>`, `branch refs/heads/<name>` or `detached`, optionally `locked [reason]` and `prunable <reason>`), blocks separated by an empty line.

**Startup refusal style (src/launch/preflight.ts:71-76, src/runner/startup.ts:74-77):**
```typescript
try {
  startingCommit = await currentHead(repo);
} catch {
  throw new Error("the repository has no commits yet; commit something before running");
}
...
if (existsSync(path.join(runDir, "state.json"))) {
  throw new UsageError(`run ${runId} already exists in ${path.dirname(runDir)}`);
}
```
Use plain `Error` for both new checks (they are environment problems, not argument mistakes). The CLI prints `error: <message>` to stderr and exits 2 for any thrown error (`src/cli.ts` lines 357–365), so no exit-code wiring is needed.

**Test: no-identity environment.** `vi.stubEnv` exists in vitest 3 and accepts `undefined` to delete a variable; execa children inherit `process.env` at call time:
```typescript
import { vi } from "vitest";
async function withoutIdentity(repo: string): Promise<void> {
  const home = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "no-identity-home-"));
  await execa("git", ["config", "--unset", "user.name"], { cwd: repo });
  await execa("git", ["config", "--unset", "user.email"], { cwd: repo });
  // Without this, git may auto-detect user@<fqdn> on some machines and succeed.
  await execa("git", ["config", "user.useConfigOnly", "true"], { cwd: repo });
  vi.stubEnv("HOME", home);
  vi.stubEnv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", home);
  vi.stubEnv("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM", "1");
  for (const v of ["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL", "EMAIL"]) vi.stubEnv(v, undefined);
}
afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllEnvs());
```
For CLI tests (child process), pass the same variables in execa's `env` instead (`{ HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: home, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: undefined, ... }`; Node ignores `undefined` values, which unsets the inherited ones — the repo already relies on this, see `RUN_ENV_UNSET` in `src/state/paths.ts`).

**Test: leftover worktree (mirrors src/runner/startup.test.ts:18-24):**
```typescript
const outside = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "leftover-"));
await rm(outside, { recursive: true });
await execa("git", ["worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", `graph-task/${RID}/2`, outside], { cwd: repo });
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `src/git/git.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function gitIdentityProblem(cwd: string): Promise<string | undefined>`: for each of `GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` and `GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT`, run `execa("git", ["var", name], { cwd, reject: false })`; on a non-zero exit return the last non-empty line of stderr (e.g. `fatal: unable to auto-detect email address (got 'root@vm.(none)')`), or `git var <name> failed` when stderr is empty. Return `undefined` when both succeed. Both are needed: the agents' commits and the runner's own `git merge --no-ff` commits need author AND committer (`GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` alone leave the committer unknown — verified).
- **IMPLEMENT**: `export interface WorktreeEntry { path: string; branch?: string; prunable: boolean }` and `export async function listWorktrees(repo: string): Promise<WorktreeEntry[]>` parsing `git worktree list --porcelain` (empty array when git fails). `branch` is the short name (without `refs/heads/`), absent for a detached worktree; `prunable` is true when the block has a `prunable` line.
- **PATTERN**: `src/git/git.ts:140-149` (`listBranches`), `src/cleanup/scan.ts:58-68`.
- **IMPORTS**: `execa` is already imported.
- **GOTCHA**: do not change `addWorktree`/`removeWorktreeIfPresent` behaviour; do not refactor `src/cleanup/scan.ts`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### UPDATE `src/launch/preflight.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function assertGitIdentity(repo: string): Promise<void>` — calls `gitIdentityProblem(repo)`; when it returns a problem, throw `new Error(...)` with this message (keep the wording; tests match parts of it):
  ```
  git has no commit identity, so no agent could commit (<problem>). Set one, then run again:
    git config --global user.name "Your Name"
    git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
  (drop --global to set it for this repository only, or set GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL)
  ```
- **IMPLEMENT**: call `await assertGitIdentity(repo)` in `checkEnvironment` right AFTER the "no commits yet" try/catch (after line 76) and before `currentBranch`. Call it also in `preflightResume` right after `const repo = await checkRepo(opts.cwd);` (line 147).
- **IMPLEMENT**: `export async function assertNoLeftoverWorktrees(repo: string, runId: string, ownWorktreesDir?: string): Promise<void>` — lists `listWorktrees(repo)` and keeps the entries whose `branch` is `graph/<runId>` or starts with `graph-task/<runId>/`, skipping `prunable` entries (their directory is gone; `git worktree prune` reclaims them) and, when `ownWorktreesDir` is given, entries whose path is inside it. If any remain, throw `new Error(...)`:
  ```
  run <runId> cannot start: its branches are still checked out in leftover worktrees:
    <path> (<branch>)
  Remove them (this deletes any uncommitted changes in them), then run again:
    git worktree remove --force <path>
    git branch -D <branch>
  ```
  one `<path> (<branch>)` line and one pair of commands per leftover worktree. Use the exact branch names `graph/${runId}` / `graph-task/${runId}/` (import `integrationBranchName`/`taskBranchName` from `src/runner/run.ts` is NOT allowed — it would create an import cycle via `startup.ts`; write the two string literals here).
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `preflightResume`, after `const { state } = store;` (line 150), call `await assertNoLeftoverWorktrees(repo, state.runId, path.join(runDir, "worktrees"))`. This leaves the run's own worktrees (task-*, integration, review-*) alone; `reconcile` (src/state/resume.ts:58-66) removes/cleans those as before.
- **PATTERN**: `src/launch/preflight.ts:71-76` for the throw style.
- **IMPORTS**: `import { ..., gitIdentityProblem, listWorktrees } from "../git/git.js";` and `realpathSync`/`existsSync` from `node:fs` for the path comparison.
- **GOTCHA**: compare paths after resolving symlinks on both sides (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`; git records real paths): `const real = (p: string) => (existsSync(p) ? realpathSync(p) : path.resolve(p));` then an entry is inside when `const rel = path.relative(real(ownWorktreesDir), real(entry.path));` satisfies `rel !== "" && !rel.startsWith("..") && !path.isAbsolute(rel)` (same test as `src/runner/startup.ts:62-63`).
- **GOTCHA**: keep `preflight` free of side effects (its doc comment, lines 117–121): do NOT run `git worktree prune` here — skip prunable entries instead.
- **GOTCHA**: the identity check must come after the "no commits" check: the existing test "refuses a repository with no commits" (preflight.test.ts:50-54) re-inits `.git`, which drops the local identity; on a CI machine without a global identity the message would otherwise change.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/runner/startup.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: between the `state.json` check (lines 75–77) and `await mkdir(runDir, ...)` (line 78): `await pruneWorktrees(repo);` (safe reclaim: forgets only registrations whose directory is gone), then `await assertNoLeftoverWorktrees(repo, runId);` (no `ownWorktreesDir`: a new run owns no worktree yet, so every worktree of `graph/<runId>` or `graph-task/<runId>/*` is a leftover). Then, still before `mkdir`, refuse a leftover integration branch:
  ```typescript
  if (await resolveRef(repo, `refs/heads/graph/${runId}`)) {
    throw new Error(`run ${runId} cannot start: the branch graph/${runId} is left over from an earlier run; delete it with: git branch -D graph/${runId}`);
  }
  ```
  — otherwise `createBranch` (run.ts:179) fails later with a raw git error. Leftover `graph-task/<runId>/*` branches WITHOUT a worktree are fine (`worktree add -B` resets them) and must not be refused.
- **PATTERN**: `src/runner/startup.ts:74-77`.
- **IMPORTS**: `pruneWorktrees`, `resolveRef` from `../git/git.js`; `assertNoLeftoverWorktrees` from `../launch/preflight.js`. The identity check comes for free through `checkEnvironment` (line 57).
- **GOTCHA**: `startup` is only called for a NEW run (resume goes through `preflightResume` + `reconcile`), so these checks never block a resume.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/runner/startup.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/suite/orchestrator.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `validateSuite`, before the per-feature `for` loop (line 133): `if (await isRepo(opts.cwd)) await assertGitIdentity(opts.cwd);` so the message is not prefixed with a feature name (the loop's preflight would otherwise report it as `<feature>: git has no commit identity ...`). In `resumeSuite`, right after `const repo = await repoRoot(opts.cwd);` (line 197) and before `findSuite`: `await assertGitIdentity(repo);`.
- **IMPORTS**: `assertGitIdentity` from `../launch/preflight.js` (already imports `preflight, UsageError` from there, line 7); `isRepo` from `../git/git.js` (line 6 already imports from there).
- **GOTCHA**: the suite spawns feature runs with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID` (orchestrator.ts:292-297); they go through `startup`, so they get the leftover check too. Nothing else to change there.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `withoutIdentity` (see Patterns) and `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllEnvs())`. Tests:
  - "refuses a repository without a git identity" — `await withoutIdentity(repo); await refuses(base(), /git has no commit identity/)`; also assert the message contains `git config --global user.email`.
  - "accepts an identity from the GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* env vars" — `withoutIdentity`, then `vi.stubEnv` the four vars; `preflight(base())` resolves with `kind: "run"`.
  - "accepts a repo-local identity" — `withoutIdentity`, then `git config user.name X` / `user.email x@x` in the repo; resolves.
  - "refuses --resume without a git identity" — create a run dir with `state.json` as in the existing "refuses --resume when the input changed" test (lines 69+), with matching hashes, then `withoutIdentity` and expect `preflight({ cwd: repo, resume: true })` to reject with `/git has no commit identity/`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/runner/startup.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `describe("startup with a custom runs root and run id")` add, with `const RID = "20260101-000000-abcd"` and `env: { GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID: RID }`:
  - "refuses a leftover worktree of the run's task branch, with cleanup steps, creating nothing" — add a worktree outside the repo on `graph-task/${RID}/2` (Patterns); expect `startup(...)` to reject with a message containing `cannot start`, the worktree path (use `realpathSync(outside)`), `git worktree remove --force` and `git branch -D graph-task/${RID}/2`; assert `existsSync(path.join(repo, ".graph-execution", RID))` is false and the worktree directory still exists (nothing was deleted).
  - "reclaims a leftover worktree whose folder is gone" — add the worktree, `rm -rf` its folder, then `startup` resolves with `ctx.runId === RID`, and `git worktree list --porcelain` no longer mentions the folder.
  - "refuses a leftover graph/<run-id> branch" — `git branch graph/${RID}`; expect rejection matching `/git branch -D graph\/20260101-000000-abcd/`.
  - "does not refuse a leftover graph-task branch without a worktree" — `git branch graph-task/${RID}/1`; `startup` resolves.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/runner/startup.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/cli.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: two CLI regressions, each inside `withRepo`:
  - "exits 2 before starting any task when git has no identity" — unset the repo-local identity and set `user.useConfigOnly true` (as in Patterns), then `execa("node", [cli, fixture("diamond"), "--spec", spec, "--provider", "fake"], { cwd: repo, reject: false, env: { HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: home, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: undefined, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: undefined, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: undefined, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: undefined, EMAIL: undefined } })`. Expect `exitCode` 2, stderr contains `git has no commit identity` and `git config --global user.name`, `existsSync(path.join(repo, ".graph-execution"))` is false, and `git for-each-ref refs/heads/graph refs/heads/graph-task` prints nothing.
  - "exits 2 at startup for a leftover worktree of a forced run id" — add the outside worktree on `graph-task/20260101-000000-abcd/2`, run the CLI with `env: { GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID: "20260101-000000-abcd" }`; expect exit 2, stderr contains `cannot start` and `git worktree remove --force`, no `state.json` under `.graph-execution/20260101-000000-abcd`, and no `graph/20260101-000000-abcd` branch.
- **GOTCHA**: `dist/cli.js` is rebuilt by `vitest.global-setup.ts` before the suite; when running a single file it still runs the global setup.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/cli.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/state/resume.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `describe("resume")`: "refuses a worktree of the run's branch outside the run folder, keeps its own, and resumes after cleanup" — `withRepo(undefined, { "task:1": { attempts: [fail, fail, fail] } }, ...)` with `fail = { commit: false, write: {} }` (as in "gives a failed task a fresh 3 attempts"); `start(repo)` exits 2 (task 1's worktree `task-1-a3` stays under `<runDir>/worktrees/`). Add an outside worktree on `graph-task/${runId}/2`. `resumeCli(repo)` → exit 2, stderr contains `cannot start` and the outside path, and `readState(runDir)` still shows task 1 `failed`. Then `git worktree remove --force <outside>` + `git branch -D graph-task/${runId}/2`, `writeFile(repo.script, "{}")`, `resumeCli(repo)` → exit 0 (the run's own leftover worktrees did not block the resume).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/state/resume.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `describe("runSuite")`: "refuses to start without a git identity, before creating anything" — `withRepo`, two `addFeature`s, `commitAll`, then the no-identity setup (vi.stubEnv as in Patterns, plus `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllEnvs())` or a try/finally with `vi.unstubAllEnvs()`); `runSuite({ cwd: repo, features, provider: "fake", merge: false, cliPath, log: () => {} })` rejects with `/^git has no commit identity/` (no feature-name prefix) and `existsSync(path.join(repo, ".graph-execution"))` is false. Add the same for `resumeSuite({ cwd: repo, log: () => {} })`: rejects with `/git has no commit identity/` (not "no suite to resume").
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Without any git identity (repro: `HOME=<empty dir> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, no `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`/`EMAIL`, no repo-local `user.*`), `graph-execution <tasks> --spec <spec> --provider fake` exits 2 immediately with `error: git has no commit identity, so no agent could commit (...)` and the `git config --global user.name/user.email` lines; no `.graph-execution/` folder, no `graph/*` or `graph-task/*` branch, no worktree is created, no agent runs.
- [ ] An identity from repo-local config or from the four `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` env vars passes the check; `GIT_AUTHOR_*` alone (no committer) is refused.
- [ ] `--resume`, the detached `--web` launcher, `graph-execution suite` and `graph-execution suite --resume` refuse the same way; the suite message is not prefixed with a feature name.
- [ ] With a worktree outside the run folder on `graph-task/<run-id>/<n>` and `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=<run-id>`, the run exits 2 at startup with `run <run-id> cannot start: its branches are still checked out in leftover worktrees:` listing `<path> (<branch>)` and the `git worktree remove --force <path>` / `git branch -D <branch>` commands; the leftover worktree is NOT deleted; no `state.json` and no `graph/<run-id>` branch are created.
- [ ] A registered worktree whose directory is gone is reclaimed silently (pruned) and the run starts.
- [ ] A leftover `graph/<run-id>` branch is refused at startup with `git branch -D graph/<run-id>`; a leftover `graph-task/<run-id>/<n>` branch without a worktree is not refused.
- [ ] `--resume` of a run whose own worktrees are still under `<runDir>/worktrees/` works as before (existing `src/state/resume.test.ts` tests stay green); a worktree of that run's branches outside the run folder is refused with the cleanup steps.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts src/runner/startup.test.ts src/state/resume.test.ts src/cli.test.ts src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts src/git/git.test.ts src/cleanup/scan.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
# Type / lint
npx tsc --noEmit
npx eslint .

# Tests for this slice (vitest's global setup rebuilds dist/ for the CLI tests)
npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts src/runner/startup.test.ts src/state/resume.test.ts src/cli.test.ts src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts src/git/git.test.ts src/cleanup/scan.test.ts

# Manual end-to-end check (TESTING.md: build, fresh temp repo, fake provider; never run in this worktree)
npm run build && CLI="$PWD/dist/cli.js" && FIX="$PWD/src/__fixtures__"
REPO=$(mktemp -d) && git -C "$REPO" init -q -b main && git -C "$REPO" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -q --allow-empty -m init
H=$(mktemp -d)
(cd "$REPO" && env -u GIT_AUTHOR_NAME -u GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL -u GIT_COMMITTER_NAME -u GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL -u EMAIL HOME=$H XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$H GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider fake; echo EXIT=$?)
```
